source.title: Long-Term Memory Engrams From Development to Adulthood

confidence_rationale: High-quality recent review in a specialist journal directly addressing how engram cells change in encoding/consolidation/retrieval from development to adulthood across hippocampus + cortical/thalamic partners. Supports Q-057's core framing that a memory trace passes through developmental gates before it can be reliably consolidated and retrieved. Confidence held below source quality because the paper is descriptive about WHICH gates exist; it does not isolate a single-cue-authority vs convergent-weak-input recall mechanism, so the mapping to the specific REE sub-question is interpretive.
failure_signatures: The review states that, compared with adults, much less is known about how or to what extent early-life memories undergo consolidation -- so any REE claim that fixes a specific developmental gate ordering is currently under-constrained by the biology.

Engram persistence depends on coordinated activity across hippocampus, retrosplenial cortex, mPFC and anterior thalamus; a single-region (CA3-only) account of cue-authority maturation may be incomplete.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Engram cells exist in the developing brain but their encoding, consolidation, retrieval and forgetting properties differ systematically from the adult; developmental differences in engram function contribute to infant memory generalization and infantile amnesia, and early-life consolidation is far less complete/understood than adult consolidation.
mapping.ree_translation: Supports Q-057's premise that a memory trace must pass developmental gates (encoding fidelity, consolidation, retrieval accessibility) before it can influence action release -- i.e. REE-v3's cue-authority limitation may partly reflect an immature recall regime (broad, generalizing, weakly consolidated) rather than a mature convergent-weak-input recall regime. Maps to MECH-362 (CA3 developmental anchor) and ARC-019.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The review is a synthesis of rodent + some human work and is explicitly descriptive about which gates exist; it does not operationalise 'single-cue authority' vs 'convergent-weak-input recall' as REE does, nor does it test offline integration as pruning vs consolidation. The mapping from 'immature engram retrieval' to REE's specific cue-authority instrumentation is an analogy, not a measured correspondence.
mapping.source_context: Review of memory engram literature; primarily rodent optogenetic/activity-tagging studies with human developmental memory framing; four regions (hippocampus, RSC, mPFC, ATN).

confidence_components.notes: Strong venue and recency; mapping fidelity moderate because the review frames developmental gates qualitatively. Transfer risk moderate: largely rodent engram work generalised to a computational substrate.
